original_question: For integers n and d with 3 <= d <= n + 1, describe the K-moduli space H^K_{n,d} that parametrizes K-semistable degree d hypersurfaces of dimension n.
target_in_paper: Section 2.1.1, Problem 7: the paper's nearest official formulation is “Describe the K-moduli space …”, with the notation identified in the nearby summary as \mathfrak{H}_{n,d}^K. Its intended scope is fixed by Problem 6 and the surrounding discussion on Fano hypersurfaces. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15576v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the main target very well: it fixes the same degree range 3\le d\le n+1, stays with n-dimensional degree-d hypersurfaces, and asks for an explicit description of the relevant K-moduli space rather than drifting to neighboring problems such as proving K-stability of all smooth hypersurfaces or treating complete intersections. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15576v1))
missing_details: It should say explicitly that the hypersurfaces are degree-d hypersurfaces X_d\subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}; this ambient projective-space realization is part of the nearby setup in Section 2.1.1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15576v1))

If you want the wording to be paper-faithful, it should use the paper’s notation \mathfrak{H}_{n,d}^K rather than a plain H^K_{n,d}. ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/review/open-problems-in-k-stability-of-fano-varieties))

The phrase “K-moduli space” should be understood in the precise Theorem 4 sense: a separated proper good moduli space arising from the relevant finite-type Artin stack, not just an informal parameter space. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15576v1))

Accordingly, “parametrizes K-semistable hypersurfaces” is slightly loose: the K-semistable objects live in the stack-theoretic moduli problem, while the K-moduli space is the associated good moduli space. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15576v1))

The draft leaves implicit why the range 3\le d\le n+1 is the one under discussion: this is exactly the Fano hypersurface range treated in Section 2.1.1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15576v1))

The nearby sentence before Problem 7 says that the general points of the K-moduli space parametrize general smooth n-dimensional hypersurfaces of degree d; including this helps make clear that the problem asks for the compactified K-moduli, not merely the open smooth locus. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15576v1))

Your draft does not state any base field or characteristic assumptions. The paper separately notes that K-stability and K-polystability do not depend on the ground field in the relevant sense, but this remains implicit in your version. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15576v1))
refined_question: For integers n and d with 3\le d\le n+1, let \mathfrak{H}_{n,d}^K denote the K-moduli good moduli space attached to the K-semistable degree-d hypersurfaces X_d\subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}, whose general points correspond to general smooth n-dimensional degree-d hypersurfaces. Give an explicit description of \mathfrak{H}_{n,d}^K. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15576v1))
justification: The exact nearest official target is Problem 7 in Section 2.1.1. The sentence immediately before it explains that general degree-d hypersurfaces are K-stable in the generic case and therefore there is a K-moduli space whose general points parametrize general n-dimensional degree-d hypersurfaces. Theorem 4 earlier in Section 2 gives the formal meaning of “K-moduli” as a separated proper good moduli space. So your draft is already close, but to make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful it should explicitly mention hypersurfaces in \mathbb{P}^{n+1}, use the paper’s notation \mathfrak{H}_{n,d}^K, and phrase the object as the K-moduli good moduli space rather than only as a space “parametrizing K-semistable hypersurfaces.” ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15576v1))
